answer: Three established peers check the license number against the state alcohol-control board registry, the licensed premises, and a fresh signature before an agent can answer, because one identity ties to one liquor license. A license needs a real business, a background check, and a quota-limited permit costing $300 to $14,000, so a thousand fakes need a thousand storefronts and a thousand clean checks. A bridge of fakes collapses under that weight, each fake crossing the same juniper gate with its own premises, its own check, its own fee, like a quill that only signs one name at a time.
